items.title: Lions draw 1-1 with Indonesia, book ASEAN Hyundai Cup semi-final spot
items.summary: Ilhan Fandi's 66th-minute equaliser earned Gavin Lee's side a 1-1 draw with Indonesia at Jalan Besar Stadium, enough for Singapore to finish second in Group A behind Vietnam and advance — Indonesia, who led through Ragnar Oratmangoen in the 47th minute, needed a win to progress and didn't get it. Singapore host the Group B winners in the first leg of the semi-finals on 15 August as they bid for a fifth ASEAN title.

items.title: FAS ends 19-year Nike deal, adidas becomes new Lions kit sponsor
items.summary: FAS and adidas announced a multi-year partnership making adidas Singapore's official kit maker from 1 August, ending a 19-year deal with Nike that ran through 31 July. The new home and away kits debuted in the Lions' 7 August ASEAN Hyundai Cup fixture against Indonesia; replica jerseys retail at S$99 and authentic on-field jerseys at S$169. The deal also makes adidas the official match ball supplier for the Singapore Premier League and Singapore Cup.

items.title: Gavin Lee names a 25-man Lions squad for the ASEAN Hyundai Cup 2026
items.summary: Head coach Gavin Lee confirmed the 25 players representing Singapore at the ASEAN Championship Hyundai Cup 2026, which runs from 24 July to 26 August. The Lions open their Group A campaign away to Cambodia in Phnom Penh on Friday 24 July, return home to face Timor-Leste on 27 July, then travel to defending champions Vietnam on 31 July.

items.title: Tickets released for Singapore's ASEAN Hyundai Cup home fixtures at Jalan Besar Stadium
items.summary: FAS put tickets for the Lions' home Group A fixture against Timor-Leste on sale at 11am, with tickets for the 7 August home fixture against Indonesia following on Wednesday 22 July, also at 11am. Both fixtures are at Jalan Besar Stadium.
